---

## 1. Problem & Context

**What problem does this solve?**
A person's chosen reading text size is not kept. Every time the reader is opened, the
text returns to its default size, so anyone who needs larger or smaller text sets it
again on every visit. The cost falls hardest on the people least able to absorb it —
those who change the size because the default is hard for them to read.

**Who is affected?**
- **Someone reading saved articles in the reader:** changes the text size to something
  readable, and loses that choice the moment the reader is closed and reopened.

**What exists today?**
The reader lets a person change the text size while they are reading, and that choice
holds for as long as the reader stays open. Nothing carries it forward: reopening the
reader starts again at the default size.

---

## 2. Scope

**In Scope:**
- Keeping the reading text size a person chooses.
- Applying that kept size when the reader is opened again.
- Behaving predictably when no size has been chosen yet, or when a kept size cannot be
  read back.

**Out of Scope:**
- Adding, removing, or changing which text sizes are offered.
- Any other reader setting — the request covers text size alone.
- Carrying the chosen size between different devices or browsers. See Open Questions;
  this is excluded until that question is answered.

---

## 3. Units of Work

> Format: short imperative title naming the outcome, then a plain sentence — what
> this unit delivers and for whom.
> Priority: **Urgent** / **High** / **Medium** / **Low**

- **Unit 1 (Urgent):** Keep the chosen reading text size across reader sessions. A person
  who sets a reading text size finds the reader already at that size the next time they
  open it, instead of setting it again. This is the foundation unit — it establishes
  where the chosen size is kept and when it is applied.
- **Unit 2 (Medium):** Open at a readable size when no kept size is available. A person
  opening the reader for the first time, or whose kept size cannot be read back, gets the
  default size rather than an unset or unreadable one.

**Happy path:** Person opens the reader → changes the text size to one that suits them →
closes the reader → opens the reader again → the text is already at the size they chose.

---

## 4. Requirements

| ID | Description | Priority | Acceptance Criteria |
|----|-------------|----------|---------------------|
| FR-001 | The reading text size a person chooses is kept when they leave the reader. | Urgent | After a person changes the text size and closes the reader, the chosen size is recorded. Closing the reader without changing the size leaves the previously kept size as it was. |
| FR-002 | Opening the reader applies the kept reading text size. | High | For a person with a kept size, the reader shows text at that size from the first moment content is readable — not at the default size first and then resized. |
| FR-003 | A person with no kept size gets the default size. | Medium | On a first-ever open, the reader uses the default text size and does not fail or leave the size unset. |
| FR-004 | A kept size that cannot be read back, or is not one of the offered sizes, falls back to the default. | Medium | When the recorded size is missing, unreadable, or not an offered size, the reader opens at the default size, and the person can still change the size normally. |

**Design-system components:** not applicable — `ui_facing` is false in config and no
design system is recorded, so no component mapping is made here.

**Key constraints:**
- Accessibility: text size is an accessibility setting for some readers, so failing to
  restore it is a readability regression, not only a convenience loss.
- FR-002 requires the size to be resolved before the first paint of article text;
  otherwise the person sees a visible jump from default to chosen size.

---

## Open Questions

- [ ] Should the chosen text size follow the person across devices and browsers, or be
      kept only on the device where it was set? Owner: Max Adamsky. Scope above excludes
      cross-device until this is answered.
- [ ] Which text sizes does the reader offer, and which one is the default? FR-003 and
      FR-004 both depend on a named default. Owner: Max Adamsky.
